headline: Humphries reveals injury after Grand Slam exit
standfirst: Luke Humphries has said he played his last-16 defeat by Tom Sykes at the Grand Slam of Darts after two days of injury problems, with a trapped nerve in his shoulder reported.
body: Luke Humphries has revealed he was battling injury when he lost 10-9 to Tom Sykes in the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts. The second seed, among the pre-tournament favourites in Wolverhampton, went out in a deciding leg on Thursday night.

Humphries addressed the problem in a post on X, congratulating Sykes on an “amazing performance” and saying he was proud of how he played “with what I’ve had to go through with injury the last 48 hours”. He added that he “gave it my absolute all”.

Dartsnews reports that the issue is a trapped nerve in his right shoulder, and that he appeared to struggle when bending to pick up his darts. That diagnosis has not been confirmed by Humphries or a medical source in the material available, so it should be treated with caution.
According to the same report, Sykes was not told about the problem until after the match, though he had noticed Humphries having difficulty collecting his darts during the warm-up.
The defeat was a narrow one. Humphries missed double 10 for the match in the decider, and Sykes then took out double 18 to book a quarter-final against Michael van Gerwen.

The immediate question is how quickly Humphries can recover. Dartsnews says he is due to play in the Players Championship Finals in Minehead next week, and that he hopes to be fit for the PDC World Championship at Alexandra Palace. How serious the problem is, and whether it affects either event, has not been made clear.
